description: Learn how words look on a page. Use clear letters, sizes, and spaces. Help people find the main idea and read the details.

questionVariants: What does typography mean?
What do we plan when we use typography?
What is the job of typography?
answerVariants: Choosing how words look and where they go.
Planning the look and place of words.
Choosing letter styles, sizes, and spaces on a page.

questionVariants: What is a font?
What does the word typeface mean?
What changes when you choose a new font?
answerVariants: The style and shape of the letters.
The way the letters are drawn.
How the letters look.

questionVariants: What does a heading tell the reader?
What is the job of a heading?
How does a heading help you start reading?
answerVariants: It names the topic of a page or part.
It tells what a page or part is about.
It gives the topic before the details.

questionVariants: What does body text give the reader?
What is the job of body text?
How does body text help after a title?
answerVariants: It gives more facts about the topic.
It explains the topic in more detail.
It adds the facts that explain the main idea.

questionVariants: What does text hierarchy show?
How does hierarchy guide your eyes?
What does a clear hierarchy help you know?
answerVariants: What to notice first, next, and last.
The order in which to notice the ideas.
Which idea comes first and which details come next.

questionVariants: The title blends in. How can you help it stand out?
How can you make a title stronger than its details?
All the words look equal. How can you draw eyes to the title?
answerVariants: Make it bigger or bolder than the other words.
Use larger or thicker letters for it.
Give it more size or weight than the details.

questionVariants: What does legible mean?
A teacher says the words are legible. What does that mean?
How would you describe text that is legible?
answerVariants: The letters are easy to see and read.
You can tell the letters apart and read them.
You can read the words without a struggle.

questionVariants: What kind of font is best for a long paragraph?
Which letter style is a good choice for many sentences?
How should the letters look in a block of details?
answerVariants: Use a plain style with clear letter shapes.
Choose simple letters that are easy to tell apart.
Pick a clear, plain letter style.

questionVariants: Where might a fancy font work well?
What is a good place for a playful letter style?
When could you use a curly font that is still clear?
answerVariants: In a short title that is easy to read.
For a brief, clear title.
On a few title words that people can read.

concepts.conceptName: Use a Small Set of Fonts
questionVariants: How many font families are a good start for one page?
What is a simple plan for the number of fonts?
How can you avoid a page with too many letter styles?
answerVariants: Use one, or two with a clear job for each.
Start with one and add a second only for a reason.
Keep to one or two, each with its own job.

questionVariants: Why can very thin letters be a poor choice for small text?
What can happen to fine letter lines at a small size?
Why should small letters have strokes you can see?
answerVariants: Their lines can be hard to see.
The fine lines may seem to fade away.
People may not see the thin lines well.

concepts.conceptName: Test Text Where It Will Be Read
questionVariants: How can you check words meant to be read across a room?
How should you test the size of words on a class screen?
What should you do to test a sign meant for faraway readers?
answerVariants: Step back and try to read them from there.
Read them from where the viewers will be.
Move to the viewing distance and check the words.

questionVariants: What does line spacing control?
Which gap changes when you adjust line spacing?
What space does the line spacing setting change?
answerVariants: The gap from one row of words to the next.
The space between rows of words.
How far apart the rows of text sit.

questionVariants: Where should a heading sit compared with its own paragraph?
How can gaps show which title and details belong together?
How should you space a heading and the facts it names?
answerVariants: Keep them close, with more room before the next group.
Put them near each other and leave a bigger gap to other groups.
Use a small gap within the group and more space outside it.

questionVariants: What does alignment mean in a design?
What do you do when you align text boxes?
How does alignment place things on a page?
answerVariants: Line things up along the same edge or center.
Put things on a shared edge or center line.
Make their edges or centers line up.

concepts.conceptName: A Steady Start for Each Line
questionVariants: Why is left alignment useful for a long paragraph?
How does left-aligned text help your eyes find the next line?
Why can a long block be easier to read along a left edge?
answerVariants: Each line starts in the same place.
Your eyes return to one steady starting point.
All the rows begin at a shared left edge.

questionVariants: When can centered text work well?
What kind of text can be a good choice to center?
Where might you use words placed around a middle line?
answerVariants: For a short title, label, or invitation.
On brief labels or titles.
For a few title or invitation words.

questionVariants: A paragraph will not fit. What can you do before shrinking it?
Too many words fill the page. How can you keep them readable?
How can you fix a crowded block without making letters tiny?
answerVariants: Cut extra words or move details to another page.
Keep the key ideas and put extra details elsewhere.
Shorten the writing or split it across pages.

questionVariants: Why use the same title style on each page?
How do matching text styles help a book feel connected?
Why keep the same look for headings throughout a project?
answerVariants: Readers learn the pattern and find their way.
The familiar pattern helps readers know where to look.
The repeated pattern helps people follow the pages.

concepts.conceptName: Help Words Stand Out from a Picture
questionVariants: Words get lost on a busy photo. How can you fix that?
How can you help text that blends into a picture?
The photo behind the words makes them hard to see. What helps?
answerVariants: Move them to a plain area or add a solid box behind them.
Use a clear empty area or a plain solid area behind them.
Place them on a quiet area or on a solid text box.

questionVariants: How should you use capital letters in a long paragraph?
What should replace a block written in ALL CAPITALS?
How can you fix a paragraph that uses only capital letters?
answerVariants: Use mostly lowercase, with capitals where needed.
Use normal sentence case.
Write normal sentences with both lowercase and capitals.

questionVariants: Should a warning be hidden in tiny type?
Should needed rules be made hard to read?
How should needed conditions be shown instead of hidden?
answerVariants: Keep them clear and large enough to read.
Make the needed words easy to see.
Show them clearly instead of hiding them in tiny text.
